Bug: removed citation disappears from the source window

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"r3mus99"} -->
_Requested by **Marek** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011tBtWDLzdZao3R8jV7Ttg1?thread=cmsg_011tBtWDLzdZao3R8jV7Ttg193q4EmXyqy7wh1quiyDtpk)_

## What changes for the user
In the source window, pressing the trash button on a citation that has a web address (for example a marriage) only removed the trash icon; the row stayed in the list until saving. The row is now hidden at once, together with its address, and counts as one unsaved change.

## Cause
The window builds its rows from the citations list and then adds rows for addresses it finds in the file under places the list does not name. A citation taken out of the list fell into that second group and was drawn again, without a trash button.

## Change
- Addresses under a citation that was removed in the window are no longer drawn.
- Nothing in the GEDCOM changes before Save; the existing removal logic is unchanged.
- Typecheck and 492 tests pass. Preview on fictional data: /mnt/project-files/arbora/citation-page/removed-citation-hidden.png

fix(desktop,ios): show download cards while a turn is running

Fixes #1331

## What

When a conversation was opened mid-turn, neither Desktop nor iOS showed any download cards. That included files from turns that had already finished. Busy sub-agent threads hit this most, because their manager keeps queueing work for them.

Both clients loaded the download list only while the runtime was idle:

- Desktop: `shouldLoadTransferDownloads` returned `false` while `runtimeIsExecuting(tab.runtimeState)`.
- iOS: `refreshDownloads()` ran only when `!session.isStreaming`.

This PR removes that gate on both clients. Nothing else changes:

- The existing triggers still decide when the list reloads. On Desktop that's open, `executing` changing, or a new message. On iOS it's `isStreaming` or the newest message changing.
- Files from the running turn still appear when the turn settles.
- The owner-only check (`foreign`) stays.
- `anchorDownloadGroups` already places a group pushed mid-turn under the live reply, because an unstamped message counts as newer.

## Evidence

In an affected sub-agent thread, the first turn pushed three mp4s and finished. The manager then queued two more messages, and the next turn kept running and pushed a png. The owner opened the thread on Desktop 0.102.0 during that turn. For several minutes Desktop polled `GET /agent/conversations/:id` every 5 seconds but never requested `GET …/file-transfers/downloads`. In the database, the groups were `ready`, owned by the conversation owner, and had the thread's `sessionId`.

## Testing

- `node --test apps/desktop/src/components/agent/panel/transferDownloads.test.ts` passes, 19 of 19. The executing case now asserts that the list loads.
- There's no layout change, so no screenshots. iOS is checked by the CI build.

Fix keyboard navigation in menus opened from toolbar buttons

## References

Fixes #20190

## Code changes

Tracks the active element before pointer and keyboard interactions in the toolbar. Avoids reactivating the parent widget when an interaction moves focus ~~to a menu~~ outside the toolbar. Preserves the existing label-handling and focus behavior.

> **Added by a maintainer**
>
> - A click that leaves the focus on the page body, such as a click on empty toolbar space, still activates the parent widget.

## User-facing changes

Keyboard navigation when opening menus from toolbar buttons works because the toolbar no longer reactivates its parent widget when focus moves to an external menu.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9044cc8-df57-4f09-b539-726ff2fcc93a

> **Added by a maintainer**
>
> - An extension button that opens a widget beside its panel, such as a preview next to a notebook, now leaves the focus in the new widget after a mouse click. Enter on the same button already behaved this way. To keep the focus in the panel, the extension can add the widget with `activate: false`.
> - The file browser's "New Launcher" button leaves the focus in the new launcher again, as in 4.6. On `main`, the focus went back to the file browser.


## Backwards-incompatible changes

None.

Read mention names and grapheme extenders in the own-delimiter decline Closes #4246 The R2 own-delimiter decline (carve#4810) now leaves a mention or tag name out of the region it scans, and the word character before an inner delimiter keeps its grapheme extenders. Implements the ticket's Expected section, which is the spec model's output (carve-rs matches it after markup-carve/carve-rs#3754). - `src/parse/inline/parse-inline-session.ts`: the closer scan for `_` exempts the `_` of a mention or tag name from the decline. That `_` can still close where it may, so `_@a__b_` keeps reading `@a` as the span, as the model does. - `src/parse/inline/parse-inline-core.ts`: new `wordBeforeGrapheme`, the word test before a position that steps over combining marks, variation selectors and joiners. - `src/render-carve.ts`: the writer's inner-delimiter test uses the same word test, so an emphasis holding `é/b` is written braced and round-trips. Reproduction (the `é` is `e` + U+0301): ```carve _@a_b_ _#a_b_ x /é/b/ ``` Before: ```html

_@a_b_

_#a_b_ x

é/b

``` After: ```html

@a_b

#a_b x

/é/b/

``` No corpus row changed. Variants: 12,285 inputs (the five bare delimiters around 11 mention and tag name shapes, six base characters with one or two extenders, escaped, braced and nested forms, each in seven hosts: paragraph, quote, bullet, ordered item, heading, table cell, link label). Against the spec model at carve main `abe808f4`: 8,694 agreed before, 12,285 after, none regressed. The writer round trip (parse, write, parse) reproduces the HTML for all 12,285. Timing (parse plus render, best of 7, on a loaded machine with load 31 on 12 cores, so the numbers are noisy): mixed text 2k 32.6 -> 7.4 ms, 8k 11.9 -> 20.0 ms, 32k 45.8 -> 66.4 ms; one line of mention names 2k 7.1 -> 8.1 ms, 8k 26.0 -> 29.2 ms, 32k 103.4 -> 77.4 ms. Both stay linear; the change adds one sticky regex test per `@` or `#` in a `_` closer scan. No limit changed. Codex review (`codex review --base origin/main`, `[codex-router] gmx (weekly 67%)`): "The changes are consistent with the intended delimiter handling, and the focused tests pass. I found no actionable regression."

fix(bill): allow negative item amounts for sales and discount lines

Bill items carried @IsPositive on amount, so create, confirm and PUT rejected receipt lines with a negative value. Item amounts may now be any non-zero value within +/-MAX_MONEY_AMOUNT; the bill total stays positive.
